GEN-IDENTITY.contract: Scient Agent and a stock omp never read, write, steer or stand in for each other: state folders, variables, pipes and socket folders carry Scient's names, and so do the executable, process, log, sign-in helper and service names and the browser relay's port. Regenerated at every alignment.

GEN-WORDING.contract: The agent calls itself Scient Agent wherever a person or a model reads its words, prompts and the Python client's README included. The prompts give the model a research and coding role and match explanations to the reader's expertise. Regenerated at every alignment.

SA-RELEASE.contract: Only Scient's own workflow builds, signs and drafts releases, and only of the version right after the latest published release, whose tag publishing the draft creates; Oh My Pi's publishing and repository automation is removed, and so is its Nix packaging, which installs and configures a stock omp. A pull request merges into main only when Scient's workflow passed on it. Dependabot updates only the actions Scient's workflow uses; Oh My Pi's dependencies change through an alignment.

SA-PRODUCT.contract: Scient Agent reports its own release: scient.json names the product, its version and the exact Oh My Pi release; --version, the startup screen, completions and the User-Agent report the version, and --runtime-info reports all of it with the build id Scient's workflow stamps, the Scient commands a host may run (hostCommands) and the plugin sources a host may add with SCIENT_AGENT_ENABLE_SOURCES (enableSources).

SA-ROOT.contract: State lives under Scient Agent's config root; a host-assigned root (SCIENT_AGENT_ROOT, from the launch environment only) is authoritative, also for user config, natives, global daemons, session owners, crash logs and .env files outside it; browser state follows the active root; a sign-in helper never takes over one Oh My Pi registered.

SA-DISCOVERY.contract: A host can add foreign user discovery sources with SCIENT_AGENT_ENABLE_SOURCES, unioned with enabledProviders only for discovery; disabledProviders wins and settings reads and writes never acquire the environment additions. SA-ROOT's dotenv protections apply.

SA-NATIVE-CACHE.contract: An absolute SCIENT_AGENT_ROOT keeps the native cache under that root regardless of SCIENT_AGENT_NATIVES_DIR. A compiled binary with a matching embedded manifest loads only its selected addon and, on modern x64, its own baseline. Oh My Pi extracts each addon into a folder named for its content. Each use refreshes the folder before loading, including a cache hit. Another build on the same package version may prune the folder after a week unused.

SA-SERVICES.contract: Oh My Pi's self-updater and its background auto-update, startup update check, startup marketplace refresh and automatic issue reports stay off; a host or installer replaces the executable.

SA-RPC-START.contract: Over RPC the agent starts without a model; a host signs in and picks one afterwards. An explicit unresolvable --model still ends the run.

SA-AUTH.contract: A host sees each sign-in's kind, whether it is stored and the store it shares; sign-out over RPC removes it or fails; a broker's sign-ins stay with the broker; a sign-in completed in another process reaches a running session.

SA-WORKER.contract: Oh My Pi's per-user daemon, which hosts the shared workers (tiny model, embeddings, word prediction), names its build by Scient Agent's release, so a newer release always has an older release's daemon re-exec into it and drop its workers, whatever the binaries' file times. Oh My Pi's package version, which two Scient Agent releases on one Oh My Pi release share, would leave the order to the binaries' modification times.

SA-BRAND.contract: Pages a person sees (the sign-in result page, the stats dashboard) carry Scient Agent's symbol and colors.

SA-POLICY.contract: An agent working here reads SCIENT.md first, and its rule on keeping Scient's changes apart comes before Oh My Pi's guidance; Scient accepts AI-assisted pull request descriptions, and the contributor stays responsible for them. Its pull requests meet SCIENT.md's definition of done.

SA-SECURITY.contract: Security reports for Scient Agent go to Scient privately, by email or a private advisory on ScientFactory/scient-agent, never to Oh My Pi's maintainer or advisories.

SA-BUILD.contract: Scient builds the native addon with cargo on the pinned toolchain: stable expressions where Oh My Pi's Bazel build allows unstable ones.

SA-RPC-SPOOL.contract: The RPC output spool, where frames wait while a host is not reading, stops the agent once it passes 2 GiB (PI_RPC_SPOOL_MAX_BYTES) instead of filling the disk, and its folder names the owning process, so an agent that starts removes the spools of agents that were killed. Proposed to Oh My Pi as can1357/oh-my-pi#16139.

SA-EXPORT.contract: An HTML export from a compiled Scient Agent carries Scient's viewer inside the page: the viewer Oh My Pi hosts is Oh My Pi's, and Scient's differs by its wording, so its checksum would not match. The wording generator refreshes the pin in viewer.generated.json.

SA-HOST-PAGES.contract: A host with its own browser sets SCIENT_AGENT_HOST_PAGES=1: the stats dashboard then reports its address, and the agent opens no system browser beside the host.

SA-SHELL-TRACE.contract: The bash tool records no execution trace unless the user turns the shell visualization on: Scient Agent's host draws none, and every live frame of a running command would carry the whole trace, up to megabytes, to the host and the session file.

SA-ASK-FORM.contract: An RPC host that enables set_ask_dialog receives the ask tool's form on one ask card. Choices carry their options and recommendation, text fields accept free text, and the question text includes the form's other content. A field that fails validation returns on the card with the reason. Other hosts receive Oh My Pi's whole form request.

SA-NEXT-MESSAGE.contract: A host asks for Oh My Pi's composer prediction of the user's next message with predict_next_message, which runs outside the command queue, so a prediction never delays the next prompt, and a turn or compaction that starts cancels it. It is Oh My Pi's prompt and reply parsing on the session's model and context; the session's history is not changed and the request is recorded in its usage. The host's own switch decides whether to ask.

SA-MAC-GRANT.contract: On macOS a Screen Recording or Accessibility grant made while the agent runs counts at once, with no restart: macOS keeps each process's first answer, so when the agent's own answer is no, a short-lived child process asks again before computer control refuses. The child's checks never prompt; a refusal is reused for two seconds and a grant for the life of the process. A general fix, to be offered upstream.

SA-AX-QUIET.contract: On macOS the agent sends no Accessibility (AX) message while it is not trusted: making an application element, the AX hit-test behind window probes, and the AXHidden read before showing an application all check trust first, without a prompt. An AX message from an untrusted process makes macOS ask for Accessibility, so a computer call that refuses for lack of a permission raised that prompt. Only the host asks. Probes then answer nothing, as they do when an application doesn't answer. A general fix, to be offered upstream.

SA-USAGE-RESET.contract: A prompt_result for a usage-limited turn carries error.resetAt, the epoch ms at which the provider said the limit resets: its retry hint, the account's usage report, or an earlier provider-stated block, whichever is latest. A stated time is read from "resets at <time>" as well as upstream's "reset at <time>", by recovery too. It is absent when the provider gave no time; the heuristic wait for a hintless error is never reported. A usage-limited failure that arrived without an HTTP status reports error.httpStatus 429, so a host that keys its usage-limit state on 429 shows it; a status the provider sent is never replaced. Hosts that do not read it are unaffected. The "resets at" reading is a candidate to propose to Oh My Pi.

SA-FAILURE-KIND.contract: A prompt_result for a failed turn carries error.kinds, the error classifier's labels for that failure (one label per AIError.Flag: auth-failed, context-overflow, transient, usage-limit, ...), plus network when the request never reached the provider: no HTTP status and Oh My Pi's network diagnosis (classifyNetworkCause, or a sentence networkFailureMessage wrote) names a DNS, connection, offline or certificate failure. It is absent when no kind is recognized. The labels are the classifier's closed vocabulary and carry no provider text. Hosts that do not read it are unaffected.

SA-ACCESS-POLICY.contract: A provider's refusal to serve a model outside the apps it lists (OpenRouter's 403 "... is only available on agentic harnesses ...") classifies as AIError.Flag.AccountPolicy, as Anthropic's organization denials do, so recovery walks the fallback chain and a host reports account-policy instead of only a failed sign-in. Another 403 stays a failed sign-in. A candidate to propose to Oh My Pi.

SA-CCA-STRING-ENUMS.contract: A tool schema sent to Cloud Code Assist in the legacy parameters field (Claude models on Google Antigravity) keeps an enum only when every value is a string, as the Gemini parametersJsonSchema path already does: Google's function declarations take string enums only and reject the whole request for any other (400 "Invalid value at ...enum[0] (TYPE_STRING), -1"). The node keeps its type, given or inferred. A candidate to propose to Oh My Pi.

SA-WEBMCP-FEATURE.contract: Every Chromium the agent launches enables the WebMCP feature beside WebMCPTesting and DevToolsWebMCPSupport. Chrome 157 and newer expose document.modelContext to pages only under WebMCP; older Chromes ignore the unknown name and keep using WebMCPTesting. Drop this when Oh My Pi enables WebMCP itself.
SA-WEBMCP-FEATURE.disposition: Oh My Pi 18.20.3 enables WebMCP itself: launch.ts launches Chromium with --enable-features=WebMCP,WebMCPTesting,DevToolsWebMCPSupport, the exact flag this hook added. Retired with the 18.20.3 alignment; upstream's browser-open-options test covers it.

SA-LIVE-HOST-DELEGATION.contract: live_connect accepts hostDelegation. When it is true, each request the realtime model delegates goes to the host as a live_delegation frame ({ text }) instead of starting a turn in the session; the host sends it as the user's message, and the live session reads that turn's progress and final answer as before. A host that runs the turn somewhere else, such as another session, reports it with live_report ({ text, final? }): progress as commentary, and with final the answer, which ends the delegation; a report without an active delegation is dropped. Without the flag, delegation is unchanged.

SA-CHATGPT-APPS.contract: The person's ChatGPT apps (Gmail, Google Drive and the others they connected in ChatGPT) through the stored openai-codex sign-in, from the MCP server the Codex apps use (chatgpt.com/backend-api/ps/mcp), with the shared OAuth retry refreshing or rotating the credential. `scient-agent apps [--json]` lists the connected apps as {"apps":[{"id","name","description"?,"tools","readOnlyTools"}]}, or prints {"error":{"kind","message"}} and exits 1, the kind being signed-out or unavailable. A host that sets SCIENT_AGENT_CHATGPT_APPS (`all`, app ids, `-<id>` to leave one out) gets the chosen apps' tools registered at session start as discoverable tools named <app>__<tool>; ChatGPT's own connector_openai_* features are never listed or registered. On a name collision, an already registered extension keeps the canonical name and the ChatGPT tool remains callable under a chatgpt__ fallback name. Without the variable nothing changes.

SA-DICTATION.contract: `scient-agent dictate <file> [--language xx] [--json]` transcribes a recording with ChatGPT's dictation service, the one the ChatGPT and Codex apps use, through the stored openai-codex sign-in, which the shared OAuth retry refreshes or rotates. With --json it prints {"text"} on success, or {"error":{"kind","message"}} and exits 1, the kind being signed-out, invalid-audio, rate-limited or unavailable. Nothing else changes.

SA-PROMPT-CACHE.contract: An assistant reply's message_end frame carries promptCache ({ tier, touchedAt, ttlMs }), the prompt-cache entry the reply's response confirmed, while the next request would still read it. It is absent for an inferred entry, a changed conversation, a model without a declared lifetime, and a cache that never expires. Each time an active warming run stops, by any cause, a cache_warming_stopped frame names the reason, stamps stoppedAt (epoch ms at the agent, independent of delivery time), and carries the same confirmed entry as warming left it (touchedAt is the last refresh that hit), absent on the same terms, so a host compacts an idle conversation on a five-minute cache while it is still warm. The agent's own idle compaction stays off over RPC, so a host that compacts before the entry expires never races it. Hosts that do not read these are unaffected.

SA-BROWSER-DEADLINE.contract: Native Tern target resolution uses one absolute deadline across selector lookup, actionability reads, scrolling and retry waits. Expiry cancels pending reads and rejects late replies before they authorize input, retaining the last recorded actionability failure. Earlier backend errors, parent cancellation and quick-read-only backend flags retain their existing semantics. Oh My Pi 18.22.0 stops before a retry round its remaining time cannot cover; a late reply that authorizes input and a pending read that outlives the action still need an upstream fix. Upstream tests remain unchanged.

SA-PLAN-MODE.contract: An RPC host can plan with the agent: the plan command (op get, enter or exit) turns plan mode on or off. In plan mode the agent changes nothing but its plan file until it proposes the plan through xd://propose. The proposal sends a plan_proposed frame (title, planFilePath, markdown), then asks the host to approve it with a select request while the tool call waits. Only an explicit approve leaves plan mode, and the same run goes on to carry out the plan; Refine asks the host what to change (an input request), and that answer, like any typed answer, reaches the model as feedback; planning goes on. An answer that arrives after plan mode was left never approves, and a new, switched or forked conversation leaves plan mode. Each time plan mode turns on or off, a plan_updated frame ({ enabled, planFilePath? }) tells the host. Planning is refused while a goal is set. Hosts that do not send plan are unaffected.

SA-RELAY-CONNECT.contract: Overlapping connection attempts share one discovery relay connection. A delayed hello from a previous link cannot replace the current tab list and strand a tab while its debugger is attaching.
SA-RELAY-CONNECT.disposition: Oh My Pi 19.1.1 replaced the extension's direct WebSocket with a native messaging port. connectRelay() records the port synchronously, so another call reuses it. Writing the instance id no longer reconnects. Each linked notification creates a new epoch, and the worker checks that epoch after building the hello. Side-panel hellos are also bound to their own port. Retired with the 19.1.1 alignment.

SA-CONTEXT.contract: When read is active, the command catalog groups described services, with at most 4,000 UTF-8 bytes of command names per row and 8,000 overall. Larger rows show a count. Read-only help://services/<key> pages list live remote names, exact commands and summaries. Bash provides schema-derived --help and execution. Explicitly inlined help, undescribed services and sessions without read retain upstream command discovery. Grouped command names and their wire aliases remain callable through eval without repeating in its advertised list. The computer manual loads at help://eval/computer or inline without read. Computer policy stays in the system prompt.

SA-CODEX-PLUGINS.contract: The opt-in user source codex-plugins (enabledProviders or SCIENT_AGENT_ENABLE_SOURCES; codex does not imply it) loads the skills and MCP servers of the Codex plugins enabled in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml (CODEX_HOME exactly as set, which must be a folder and is canonicalized, else ~/.codex), merged at every depth over Codex's system config.toml (/etc/codex, or OpenAI\Codex in the ProgramData known folder), a table without enabled taking [plugins._default]. Nothing loads while [features] plugins is anything but true when set, or when the merged [plugins] table has a field of a type Codex rejects (PluginsConfigToml, apps' AppConfig included), as in Codex. CODEX_HOME, header credentials and servers' variables come from getLaunchEnv() (packages/utils env.ts: the exec environment from procfs or --no-env-file, or the compiled binary's environment before the agent's .env files load, the binary marked by __SCIENT_AGENT_NO_DOTENV__, which only scripts/compile-binary.ts defines, beside autoloadDotenv false; never with an explicit --env-file), never a .env file; when it is unknown nothing loads, with a warning. It reads the version Codex runs in $CODEX_HOME/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<name>/ with Codex's manifest precedence: a root Agent Plugins plugin.json (its skills/ and a regular-file mcp.json, read under that standard, sse servers left out, a stdio server taking the env_vars a valid .codex-plugin declaration of the same server as a valid stdio server adds), else .codex-plugin, .claude-plugin or .cursor-plugin/plugin.json, a link or non-file there, a linked folder holding it, or a field of a type Codex rejects rejecting the plugin. Manifest paths Codex does not take (not ./-relative, rooted, or holding .., a backslash separating parts only on Windows) are dropped, falling back as in Codex to skills/ and .mcp.json; paths it takes must resolve inside the package. Skills are found as Codex scans (every SKILL.md six levels down for a legacy plugin, direct children for an Agent Plugins package, hidden folders skipped), each folder and SKILL.md resolved inside the package before it is read, carry containRoot so skill:// stays in the package and the plugin ID as their plugin name, take their frontmatter name, or else their folder's, with its Unicode whitespace collapsed as Codex does, and follow the user config's [[skills.config]] rules in Codex's order (an absolute path, canonicalized, or a name trimmed of Unicode whitespace matching the name Codex gives the skill, <manifest name>:<skill>, the package folder's name standing in for a manifest name of Unicode whitespace or nothing; a [skills] table Codex cannot read gives no rules). A server whose declared name does not match Codex's ^[a-zA-Z0-9_:@/.-]+$ (validate_mcp_server_name) is skipped, as Codex refuses to start it. A legacy server must declare exactly one transport, only that transport's Codex fields, every field of the type Codex accepts (durations as Rust's Duration and u64 take them), and no other Codex environment; cwd and relative commands must stay inside the symlink-resolved package. Every imported server's tool calls have a hard cap, its tool_timeout_sec or else Codex's 300-second default, in both formats (MCPServer and MCPServerConfig toolTimeoutMs, honoured by resolveMCPRequestDeadline in mcp/timeout.ts for the stdio, http and sse transports, never extended by a call's own wait arguments or progress); one monotonic deadline (MCPRequestOptions.deadlineAt, on performance.now()) starts before argument preparation and holds through input-required rounds, credential refresh, reconnect and every replay. The outermost caller arms the timer once. The local host checks the deadline on arrival and carries it on the request signal through lazy startup and header discovery. The writer checks it after preparation, before handing a frame to native stdio or sending an HTTP/SSE POST, including redirects. A stalled wait ends at that deadline with a nonretryable timeout. Bytes already handed to native stdio may drain later; a server with tool_timeout_sec = 0, whose every tool call Codex times out, is skipped. Every server this source imports uses the in-process MCP host even when sharing is enabled. Its unit, era probe and catalogs share only with an imported definition of the same upstream identity, complete child environment and bound credential ID. A stdio server's env is what Codex would give it (its variable list, certificate bundles as absolute paths, its env_vars, then its literal env, without Codex's non-inheritable names in any case) and it inherits nothing else (MCPServer.envInherit = []); an HTTP server carries literal, origin-locked headers set in Codex's order, each replacing a header of the same name in any case, a header whose name is not an HTTP token or whose value has characters other than tab and visible ASCII skipped (http_headers, env_http_headers values used as set unless only Unicode whitespace, then the bearer_token_env_var value, which must be set, non-empty and a valid header value or the server is skipped, as Codex refuses to start it), and its OAuth client settings, scopes (an empty list kept) and oauth_resource. Its oauth table is read as Codex reads a plugin's: the camelCase aliases clientId, clientSecret, callbackUrl and callbackPort fold into their snake_case keys by key presence, a present snake_case key winning even when null, before any type is checked. The server is skipped, as Codex refuses to start it, when its client secret is present without a client ID or either of them is blank by Rust's Unicode White_Space (an empty secret included), or when it sets authorization_server_issuer or token_endpoint_auth_method, which Codex allows only with ema_auth; a blank client ID without a secret counts as none; and a client ID or secret with surrounding whitespace, which Scient Agent's sign-in would trim where Codex keeps it, skips the server too. An HTTP server signs in under its own credential, as Codex keys sign-ins by server name and URL: auth.credentialId is mcpOAuthServerCredentialId (mcp/oauth-flow.ts, mcp_oauth:server:<profile>:<encoded name>:<url>, which the profile and URL parsers read). Only the codex-plugins source binds one: trustedMcpAuth (mcp/oauth-flow.ts) drops a server-bound id from any definition but the one that source imported under the id its name and URL give, in mcp/config.ts, at every MCPManager connection (mcp/manager.ts, judged by the source supplied with that definition, never one an earlier definition left registered under the name) and in /mcp test, where the provenance is the selected definition's own (the TUI controller takes the live source only for a discovered selection and connects the tested definition to the manager with that source alone; slash-commands/helpers/mcp.ts reads config files, which never bind); a malformed non-string id is left alone. mcp/oauth-credentials.ts answers a bound id only for its own URL under the active profile and, when the server configures a confidential OAuth client (a client secret), only for a credential made with exactly that client ID (Codex asks for a fresh sign-in on another one; credentials that are not server-bound are looked up as before, whatever the client settings hold), never falls back from it to the URL-keyed row, and lets a configured Authorization header win over it. Like Codex, a server-bound sign-in stores no client secret and follows no token-endpoint redirect: the sign-in flow (mcp/oauth-reauth.ts) keeps none and its code exchange refuses redirects (MCPOAuthConfig.rejectRedirects); every refresh path, the manager's, `omp token`'s and the auth broker's (cli/auth-broker-cli.ts), names the row to refreshManagedMcpOAuthCredential, which for a bound row sends the stored client ID with only the secret the current definition configures (the manager passes it; callers without a definition send none), never a stored or retired one, and refuses redirects (refreshMCPOAuthToken's rejectRedirects, whose trailing options are read whether or not a resource is given); reauthorization likewise takes its secret from the current definition only. A secret an earlier build of this change left on a bound row is never sent; the broker's generic merge may keep it on the row. Reauthorization and TUI /mcp unauth act on a bound id only for a discovered server whose name and URL give it, and a sign-in challenge from a live imported server is answered for that live definition, never a same-named config-file entry. A server declaring bearer_token_env_var is bound with auth.type apikey, so no sign-in answers it and reauthorization refuses it, as Codex never offers it OAuth login. Reauthorization takes a bound server's values literally, asks for its configured scopes (an empty list meaning none, discovery's scope parameter dropped) and its oauth_resource before a discovered one, stores the credential under that id and writes nothing back; reconnecting keeps its auth block and headers and matches only a manager entry with the same credential id; TUI /mcp unauth (modes/controllers/mcp-command-controller.ts) removes only its own credential and rewrites no config, and /mcp enable and disable toggle an imported server through disabledServers. Servers are named <plugin>@<marketplace>:<server>, so another plugin's arrival never renames one and settings keyed by the name stay put. Left out with a warning: a plugin server the config's own [mcp_servers] names, as Codex runs that entry instead; servers two enabled plugins declare under one name, since Codex runs only one of them; and a server whose declaration or plugin mcp_servers.<name> table says enabled = false or has an ema_auth key, so no enabledServers entry can start it. Skipped with a warning while siblings load: servers whose tools Codex narrows (enabled_tools, or a non-empty disabled_tools), hides from the model (a non-empty omit_tools_from), caps (tools.<name>.output_token_limit) or asks about regardless of its session policy (default_tools_approval_mode or tools.<name>.approval_mode of prompt or writes; auto defers, like Scient Agent's approval mode, to the session's policy), which Scient Agent cannot enforce, and servers with malformed or unsupported fields (http_headers_helper, auth other than oauth). OpenAI host-only plugins (browser, chrome, codex-app-tools, computer-use, unified-computer-use from openai-bundled), servers launched by computer-use-client-launcher or signed in with Codex's ChatGPT session, app references and hooks are not loaded, and nothing loads while an organization policy manages Codex or a policy location cannot be checked (requirements.toml in the system folder or at the 64-bit Group Policy RequirementsPath, both read on Windows through one PowerShell query that stops on any error, only its explicit success counting as no policy; /etc/codex/managed_config.toml; macOS managed preferences for com.openai.codex). Not applied: Codex profiles, project .codex/config.toml layers and cloud-delivered config. Known gaps: servers whose names differ only in characters that tool names drop (twin.a@m:api and twin-a@m:api) mint the same tool names, and the registry keeps one; a JSON timeout written 1.0 passes where Codex's u64 field rejects it. A host shows and signs in to MCP servers through scient-agent mcp (scient/mcp-command.ts, registered in cli-commands.ts and listed in --runtime-info hostCommands), which discovers with the user's settings bound (initializeWithSettings), so enabledProviders and disabledProviders apply as in a conversation: mcp list [--server <name>] uses the configured sharing and idle policy, extension roots, project opt-in and built-in transforms, and probes each enabled server on a fresh attachment with live discovery and tool listing and prints one JSON line of its status (connected with its tool count, needs-auth when an http or sse server answers with an auth challenge, failed, or pending when the startup window closes first), scope, plugin ID and whether a browser sign-in serves it (canSignIn in scient/mcp-sign-in-pickup.ts: http or sse, no Authorization header, and for a bound server only auth.type oauth); mcp login <name> runs the reauthorization /mcp reauth runs on the definition discovery selected (an imported server's from the manager, never a same-named config-file entry it shadowed; an ordinary server's from the file holding that same definition), printing the authorization URL as a JSON line for the host to open (it opens no browser itself), then completed or failed. Every message either command prints is written there, an HTTP status at most, never a server's or authorization server's own text, which can echo a token, a code or a secret. While a broker holds the sign-ins, a bound server that configures a client secret is neither offered (no canStartSignIn) nor signed in to (reauthorization refuses it in mcp/oauth-reauth.ts), since the broker refreshes without the definition and so without the secret. In RPC mode (modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts) an McpSignInPickup, seeded with the sign-ins the session started with, runs before each prompt and checks servers a browser sign-in serves, including a cached-ready attachment that survived a live auth failure. It reconnects with live discovery and tool listing once the stored sign-in differs from the one it started with or last tried, so a refused sign-in is not retried every prompt; one pickup runs at a time, a prompt waits for it at most 1.5 seconds while the rest finishes in the background, a broker's sign-ins are re-read at most every 10 seconds, and the session's tools are refreshed when a server connects. Unchanged from Oh My Pi and the same for every MCP server: the transport's connection error and the token exchange's error carry the response text, and a failed refresh is logged with its error.
